_comment: Auxiliary — read-only AWS describe/get output for s3://4shark-terraform-state, collected 2026-07-15 with the default (read-only) profile. Referenced by PLAN-SPIKE.md findings F10-F13. Each block is the verbatim response of the named command.

get-bucket-encryption._reading: SSE-S3 (AES256), NOT SSE-KMS. Encrypted at rest, but decryption is transparent to any principal holding s3:GetObject on the object — there is no separate KMS key policy acting as a second authorization gate. Access control is therefore entirely IAM identity policy.

get-public-access-block._reading: All four public-access blocks are on. The bucket cannot be made public by ACL or policy.

get-bucket-policy._response_stderr: An error occurred (NoSuchBucketPolicy) when calling the GetBucketPolicy operation: The bucket policy does not exist
get-bucket-policy._reading: No resource policy exists. Combined with SSE-S3 (no KMS key policy), the ONLY thing standing between a principal and the plaintext state is its IAM identity policy. Who currently holds s3:GetObject on this bucket was NOT enumerated in this spike — see PLAN-SPIKE.md open questions.

get-bucket-versioning._reading: Versioning is ENABLED. Consequence for rotation: replacing a datadog_api_key writes a new state object version, but every PRIOR object version still contains the OLD key value in plaintext-readable form. Rotating the key in Datadog makes the old value useless, so this is not a live exposure — but a rotation done because a key LEAKED does not erase that key's value from S3 history. Only lifecycle expiration of noncurrent versions, or explicit version deletion, does.

_not_researched: Which IAM principals currently hold s3:GetObject on 4shark-terraform-state — not enumerated. This is the actual blast radius of the state-exposure trade-off and is answerable with read-only IAM calls, but was out of the scope reached in this spike.
Whether CloudTrail data events are enabled for this bucket (HashiCorp's 'Use audit logs to track state access over time' recommendation). Not checked.
Whether a noncurrent-version expiration lifecycle rule exists on the bucket. Not checked — relevant to how long an old key value persists in object history.
